title: Erdős Problem #633: Square Number Triangle Dissections
description: Which triangles can ONLY be cut into a perfect square number of congruent triangles? Classification remains OPEN with $25 prize.

meta.assumptions: 0 axiom(s) and 0 sorry(s) — fully machine-checked. This entry does NOT resolve Erdős #633 (which remains OPEN, $25); instead it rigorously establishes a sharp NEGATIVE result about the natural first-attempt formalization. The area+side-ratio relaxation CongruentDissection (and its similar analogue CanDissectIntoSimilar) is too coarse to see the square-only phenomenon: by Triangle.area_scale the scaled copy T.scale (1/√n) witnesses EVERY count n ≥ 1, so dissectionCounts_eq gives DissectionCounts T = {n | 1 ≤ n} and all_similar_counts gives CanDissectIntoSimilar T n for all n ≥ 1. Consequently no_square_only_in_model (no triangle is square-only), no_exceptional_similar_in_model (no #634 exceptions survive), and the proved negations soiferTriangle_not_square_only_in_model / no_square_only_witness_in_model / squareOnly_empty_in_model. The prior 5 sorries asserted square-only statements the model actually DISPROVES (a soundness smell); they have been removed and replaced by their proved negations or honest corollaries. A faithful resolution of #633/#634 requires replacing the relaxation with a real non-overlapping tiling predicate — the hard, open core left for future work.

overview.historicalContext:
This problem concerns the geometry of triangle dissections — partitioning a triangle into congruent triangular pieces. Every triangle can be dissected into n² congruent copies by subdividing each side into n equal segments and connecting corresponding points, forming an n × n grid of congruent sub-triangles.

The question is: are there triangles where n² is the ONLY achievable dissection count? Alexander Soifer investigated this systematically in his book 'How Does One Cut a Triangle?' (2009). He showed that the triangle with sides √2, √3, √4 has this 'square-only' property — it cannot be dissected into any non-square number of congruent triangles. The key constraint comes from the irrational side lengths: any tiling must respect algebraic relationships between the sides, and the only way to achieve area compatibility with matching angles forces the count to be a perfect square.

Soifer's analysis connects to the concept of 'integral independence' of angles: if the three angles α, β, γ of a triangle satisfy no non-trivial integer linear relation (beyond α + β + γ = π), then dissection constraints force square-only counts. Equilateral triangles (angles π/3, π/3, π/3 — integrally dependent via α = β = γ) can be dissected into 3 pieces, and right isosceles triangles (π/4, π/4, π/2 — integrally dependent via α = β, γ = 2α) can be dissected into 2 pieces.

The complete classification of square-only triangles remains OPEN with a $25 Erdős prize. The conjecture is that integral independence of angles is the precise characterization.
overview.problemStatement:
**Classification Problem (OPEN, $25 prize):**

Characterize all triangles T such that: if T can be dissected into n congruent triangles, then n must be a perfect square.

**Known:**
- Every triangle can be dissected into n² copies (for any n >= 1)
- The triangle with sides √2, √3, √4 can ONLY be dissected into square counts
- Triangles with 'integrally independent' angles have this property
- Equilateral (3 pieces) and right isosceles (2 pieces) do NOT have this property

**Unknown:**
- Complete characterization of square-only triangles
- Whether integral independence is necessary and sufficient
overview.text: Which triangles can ONLY be cut into a perfect square number of congruent triangles? Classification remains OPEN with $25 prize.
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization is a fully-verified NEGATIVE (model-adequacy) result, not a resolution of the open problem:

1. **Triangle representations**: Triangle (by sides) and TriangleByAngles (by angles), with Heron area
2. **The engine**: Triangle.area_scale — Heron's area is homogeneous of degree 2 (scaling sides by t scales area by t²)
3. **Congruent relaxation collapses**: CongruentDissection captures only area + side ratios; via area_scale the scaled copy T.scale (1/√n) witnesses every n ≥ 1, so dissectionCounts_eq gives DissectionCounts T = {n | 1 ≤ n} and no_square_only_in_model shows no triangle is square-only
4. **Similar relaxation collapses identically**: all_similar_counts gives CanDissectIntoSimilar T n for all n ≥ 1, so similar_dissection_characterization is vacuous and no_exceptional_similar_in_model refutes the #634 exceptions
5. **Proved negations replace the former model-false sorries**: soiferTriangle_not_square_only_in_model, no_square_only_witness_in_model, squareOnly_empty_in_model
6. **Honest namesake**: erdos_633_model_collapse summarizes the collapse; the classification (erdos633Classification, erdos_633_open) remains OPEN and is documented as such
keyInsights: **Universal n² dissections**: Every triangle can be subdivided into n² congruent copies by grid construction — the question is whether NON-square counts are also achievable
**Soifer's example**: The triangle (√2, √3, √4) can only be dissected into square counts — irrational side lengths severely constrain tiling possibilities

**Integral independence of angles**: If no non-trivial integer relation holds between the angles, dissection constraints force square-only counts. Dependent angles (like equilateral: α = β = γ) allow non-square dissections
**Similar vs congruent**: For similar (not congruent) dissections, the problem is solved: every n except 2, 3, 5 works. The congruent case is much harder
**Open classification**: The precise characterization of square-only triangles is worth $25 — conjectured to be integral independence

sections.title: Problem Statement and Imports
sections.summary: Header docstring stating Erdős Problem #633 ($25, OPEN): classify the triangles that can ONLY be cut into a square number of congruent triangles. Notes that every triangle dissects into n² congruent copies, references Soifer's √2/√3/√4 example and the related similar-dissection Problem #634. Imports Mathlib and opens Real, Set.
sections.mathContext: Erdős #633: classify triangles whose congruent-dissection counts are exactly the perfect squares. Background: every triangle admits a dissection into $n^2$ congruent copies (the $n \times n$ scaling), so the question is which triangles admit *no* non-square count.

sections.title: Triangle Representation
sections.summary: Defines the Triangle structure (three positive side lengths with the triangle inequalities), the TriangleByAngles structure (three angles in (0,π) summing to π), and Triangle.area via Heron's formula.
sections.mathContext: A triangle is encoded by side lengths $a,b,c>0$ satisfying the three triangle inequalities, or alternatively by angles $\alpha,\beta,\gamma \in (0,\pi)$ with $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=\pi$. Area uses Heron: $\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$ with $s=(a+b+c)/2$.

sections.title: Dissection Definitions
sections.summary: Defines CongruentDissection T S n (n copies of S tile T, with an area condition and a congruence/proportionality condition), CanDissectInto T n (∃ such S), and DissectionCounts T (the set of n ≥ 1 into which T can be congruently dissected).
sections.mathContext: CongruentDissection requires $\mathrm{area}(T)=n\cdot\mathrm{area}(S)$ together with proportional side ratios. DissectionCounts$(T)=\{n\geq 1 : T$ can be cut into $n$ congruent copies$\}$.

sections.title: Square Number Property
sections.summary: Defines IsPerfectSquare n (n = k²), HasSquareOnlyProperty T (every achievable dissection count is a perfect square), and the set SquareOnlyTriangles of triangles with that property — the central object Erdős #633 asks to classify.
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{HasSquareOnlyProperty}(T) :\Leftrightarrow \forall n \in \mathrm{DissectionCounts}(T),\ \exists k,\ n=k^2$. SquareOnlyTriangles is the subset of all such $T$; the open problem is to characterize it geometrically.

sections.title: Universal Dissection into Squares
sections.summary: Triangle.scale and Triangle.area_scale (degree-2 homogeneity of Heron's area, fully verified) provide the engine. universal_square_dissection (now PROVED): every triangle dissects into n² congruent copies for any n ≥ 1, witnessed by the similar copy of linear scale 1/n. squares_always_achievable (proved from it): every perfect square ≥ 1 lies in DissectionCounts T.
sections.mathContext: The $n \times n$ scaling subdivision gives $k^2 \in \mathrm{DissectionCounts}(T)$ for all $k\geq 1$ and every triangle $T$. Thus square counts are universal; the problem is whether any *non-square* count is also achievable.

sections.title: Soifer's Example
sections.summary: Defines soiferTriangle, the triangle with sides √2, √3, √4 (= 2), discharging its positivity and triangle-inequality obligations with explicit sqrt bounds. soiferTriangle_not_square_only_in_model (PROVED) records that Soifer's genuine geometric claim is model-false in this relaxation: no_square_only_in_model already disproves HasSquareOnlyProperty soiferTriangle.
sections.mathContext: Soifer's witness has sides $\sqrt2,\sqrt3,2$; the triangle inequalities follow from $1<\sqrt2,\sqrt3<2$. It is the canonical example conjectured to be cuttable only into square numbers of congruent copies.

sections.title: Integral Independence
sections.summary: Defines HasIntegrallyIndependentAngles (no non-trivial integer combination of the angles vanishes). no_square_only_witness_in_model (PROVED) records that the heuristic 'integrally independent angles ⇒ square-only' is model-false here: the existence conclusion ∃ T', HasSquareOnlyProperty T' fails outright since no triangle is square-only in the relaxation.
sections.mathContext: Integral independence of $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ rules out the rational angle relations that enable non-square dissections, suggesting a link between angle arithmetic and the square-only property.

sections.title: Non-Square Dissections for Generic Triangles
sections.summary: Defines HasNonSquareDissection (some achievable count is not a perfect square) and gives two existence witnesses (both now PROVED via area_scale): equilateral triangles dissect into 3 copies, and right isosceles triangles (legs equal, hypotenuse = leg·√2) dissect into 2 copies — both non-square counts in the area-compatibility model.
sections.mathContext: Generic triangles admit non-square counts: equilaterals give $3\in\mathrm{DissectionCounts}$, right isosceles give $2$. These are the obstructions that a square-only triangle must avoid.

sections.title: Similar vs Congruent Dissections
sections.summary: Defines CanDissectIntoSimilar (the area+side-ratio relaxation of similar dissection) and proves it collapses just like the congruent model: all_similar_counts (CanDissectIntoSimilar T n for every triangle and every n ≥ 1). Hence similar_dissection_characterization is now PROVED with a vacuous {2,3,5} exclusion, and no_exceptional_similar_in_model refutes the model-false exceptional-cases claim (every triangle satisfies the relaxation at n = 2,3,5).
sections.mathContext: The genuine Problem #634 ($n \notin \{2,3,5\}$ with real exceptions at $2,3,5$) needs a faithful tiling. The relaxation $\mathrm{CanDissectIntoSimilar}$ used here is too coarse: by area homogeneity it holds for every $n \geq 1$, so the #634 exceptions are invisible — the same collapse that defeats the congruent model of #633.

sections.title: The Classification Problem (OPEN)
sections.summary: Defines erdos633Classification (the existence of a 'nice' geometric predicate P characterizing HasSquareOnlyProperty) and the placeholder theorem erdos_633_open (a tautology marking the problem as unresolved). The $25 prize is for a complete characterization.
sections.mathContext: The classification target: a geometric predicate $P$ with $\mathrm{HasSquareOnlyProperty}(T) \Leftrightarrow P(T)$ for all $T$. No such characterization is known; this remains the open core of Erdős #633.

sections.title: Partial Results
sections.summary: Defines soiferFamily (triangles with sides √p, √q, √r for distinct naturals satisfying the triangle inequality). squareOnly_empty_in_model (PROVED) records that the partial result 'soiferFamily ⊆ SquareOnlyTriangles' is model-false: here SquareOnlyTriangles ⊆ ∅ (no triangle is square-only) while soiferFamily is nonempty, pinning down exactly why the relaxation is too coarse.
sections.mathContext: soiferFamily $=\{T : a=\sqrt p, b=\sqrt q, c=\sqrt r,\ p,q,r$ distinct$\}$ is nonempty (it contains soiferTriangle), yet $\mathrm{SquareOnlyTriangles}=\emptyset$ in the relaxation, so the genuine containment cannot be seen without a faithful tiling predicate.

sections.title: Main Theorem Statement
sections.summary: erdos_633_model_collapse: the honest namesake theorem. Both relaxations accept all n ≥ 1 (DissectionCounts T = {n | 1 ≤ n} and CanDissectIntoSimilar T n for all n ≥ 1), so the square-only property is vacuous and any faithful resolution of #633/#634 needs strictly finer geometric data than area + side ratios. Closes with #check commands.
sections.mathContext: Top-level proven statement: $(\forall T,\ \mathrm{DissectionCounts}(T)=\{n\mid 1\le n\}) \wedge (\forall T,\ \neg\mathrm{HasSquareOnlyProperty}(T))$. This does NOT resolve #633 (still OPEN); it sharply delimits what the area+ratio relaxation can express.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #633 asks for a classification of triangles that can only be dissected into perfect square numbers of congruent triangles. Soifer showed the triangle (√2, √3, √4) has this property, connected to the concept of integrally independent angles. Counterexamples include equilateral (3 pieces) and right isosceles (2 pieces) triangles, whose angle dependence enables non-square dissections. The complete classification remains OPEN with a $25 prize.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: This problem sits at the intersection of combinatorial geometry, tiling theory, and algebraic number theory.

The formalization's contribution is a cautionary, fully-verified meta-result: the natural first-attempt encoding of 'congruent dissection' as area-compatibility plus matched side ratios is too weak to capture the square-only phenomenon at all — it (and the analogous similar-dissection relaxation) accepts every count n ≥ 1. This sharply identifies what a faithful formalization must add: an actual non-overlapping geometric tiling, not just numeric area/ratio bookkeeping. The genuine square-only constraint arises from algebraic relationships between irrational side lengths and angles (linear independence over the rationals) that the relaxation discards.
openQuestions: Give a complete characterization of square-only triangles (the $25 prize!)
Is integral independence of angles both necessary and sufficient for the square-only property?
Is the set of square-only triangles dense or sparse among all triangles?
Are there square-only triangles not in Soifer's family (sides √p, √q, √r)?

mainTheorems.name: erdos_633_model_collapse
mainTheorems.description: The honest namesake result: both the area+side-ratio relaxation DissectionCounts (= {n | 1 ≤ n} for every triangle) and its similar analogue accept ALL counts n ≥ 1, so the square-only property is vacuous. Any faithful resolution of Erdős #633/#634 must use strictly finer geometric data than area and side ratios.

mainTheorems.name: dissectionCounts_eq
mainTheorems.description: DissectionCounts T = {n | 1 ≤ n} for every triangle T — the congruent relaxation collapses to all positive integers, witnessed by the scaled similar copy T.scale (1/√n) via degree-2 area homogeneity.

mainTheorems.name: all_similar_counts
mainTheorems.description: The similar-dissection relaxation CanDissectIntoSimilar collapses identically: every triangle admits CanDissectIntoSimilar T n for all n ≥ 1. Hence similar_dissection_characterization holds trivially and the genuine Problem #634 exceptions at n = 2,3,5 are invisible to this model (no_exceptional_similar_in_model).

mainTheorems.name: no_square_only_in_model
mainTheorems.description: No triangle has the square-only property in the relaxation (the non-square count 2 is always achievable). The engine behind the proved negations soiferTriangle_not_square_only_in_model, no_square_only_witness_in_model, and squareOnly_empty_in_model that replace the file's former model-false sorries.
